title: Redux Project Structure
description: Learn how to organize a Redux codebase for maintainability with feature folders, the ducks pattern, and clear module boundaries.

data.text: The way you organize your Redux code determines how easy it is to **add features, onboard developers, and refactor**. Two popular approaches are *type-based* folders (`/reducers`, `/actions`) and *feature-based* folders (`/features/auth`, `/features/cart`).

data.title: Recommendation
data.text: For most apps, **feature folders** win. They keep everything related to one domain in one place, which matches how teams actually work.

data.title: Feature-based structure
data.content: Co-locate slice, components, and API calls
data.code:
src/
  app/
    store.ts
    rootReducer.ts
  features/
    auth/
      authSlice.ts
      LoginForm.tsx
      authAPI.ts
      authSelectors.ts
    todos/
      todosSlice.ts
      TodoList.tsx
      todosAPI.ts
      todosSelectors.ts
  components/
    Button.tsx
    Modal.tsx
  hooks/
    useAuth.ts
  utils/
    formatDate.ts

cards.title: Feature folders
cards.description: `/features/auth/authSlice.ts` — everything for one domain lives together.
cons: Shared logic needs an obvious home (e.g., `common/`)

cards.title: Type folders
cons: Touching one feature requires editing many folders

rows: createSlice with reducers and initial state
Public API — re-export what other features need

data.text: The **ducks** pattern bundles action types, action creators, and the reducer for one slice into a single file. Redux Toolkit's `createSlice` already gives you this — you no longer need separate `actions.ts` and `reducer.ts` files for the same domain.

data.title: createSlice = ducks built in

data.text: Each feature should expose a **minimal public API** through an `index.ts`. Other features import only from there, not from internal files.

data.title: index.ts as a facade
data.content: Hide internals, share only what's needed

terms.definition: A directory containing all files for one domain (auth, todos, etc.).
Bundling actions and reducer for one slice in a single module.
The set of exports another module is allowed to depend on.
Keeping related code close together so it changes together.

data.title: Scaling tip
data.text: When a folder grows past ~10 files, split it. For example, `features/orders/` might become `features/orders/{components,api,utils}`.

data.title: Restructure a type-based project
data.description: Take a project organized as `/actions`, `/reducers`, `/components`. Restructure it into `/features/<feature>` folders.
steps: Move each reducer and its related actions into one folder.
Verify nothing else in the app breaks after the refactor.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Group by feature, not by Redux type, in most apps
Each feature folder has a clear public API through `index.ts`
Use `createSlice` so actions and reducer live together (ducks)
Keep shared utilities in a top-level `common/` or `utils/` folder
Restructure before the pain sets in, not after
data.takeaway: Feature folders with public APIs scale Redux apps effectively.
